notes: Read all three units, balanced-budget context, all thirteen candidates and the review. Recast candidates two through seven as Republican-supported expenditure tests rather than actions by budgets, named U.S. constitutional and governmental scope, preserved the source's disjunctive effectiveness-or-necessity condition, and removed the kill metaphor. Named the U.S. budget and Republican actor, strengthened Medicaid to will preserve, and tied financing control to avoiding harm to elderly and needy beneficiaries.

claims.claim_text: Republicans support testing whether an expenditure falls within the U.S. federal government's constitutional scope and ending it if not.
Republicans support testing whether an expenditure was effective in the past and remains absolutely necessary, and ending it if either condition fails.
Republicans support testing whether an expenditure is important enough to justify borrowing, especially foreign borrowing, and ending it if not.
Medicare and Medicaid financing must be controlled before those programs consume most of the U.S. federal budget, including national defense.
The platform says Medicare and Medicaid financing can be controlled without endangering elderly and needy beneficiaries.
Republicans intend to save Medicare by modernizing it, empowering participants and securing its finances.
Republicans will preserve Medicaid's promise by converting a program designed for 1965 medicine into a vehicle for health in a new era.
